articles.title: Momentum vs Weather & Clock Dashboard: Which Firefox New Tab Extension Wins?
articles.excerpt: Momentum is the benchmark for new tab extensions. It's beautiful: a daily photo, a quote, a time, a focus field. It's been a standard recommendation for years. Then it went freemium. Weather moved to…
articles.body: Momentum is the benchmark for new tab extensions. It's beautiful: a daily photo, a quote, a time, a focus field. It's been a standard recommendation for years. Then it went freemium. Weather moved to Momentum Plus ($3.33/month). That's $40/year for weather on your new tab. This isn't a complaint about Momentum charging — it's a reasonable product decision. But it creates a question: for users who primarily want weather + clocks on their new tab, are there free alternatives that actually work? What I Was Looking For My requirements were simple: Current weather + at least a 2-day forecast World clocks for multiple cities Doesn't require an account Free, without hidden upgrades Momentum free tier covers: time, focus, background photo. Weather is not in the free tier.

articles.title: How I built CastRemix: swap the lead character in any short video with AI
articles.excerpt: I've been building CastRemix, a tool for AI video character swaps. What it does: you upload a short reference video (2–30s) plus a photo of your character, and it generates a new take where your chara…
articles.body: I've been building CastRemix , a tool for AI video character swaps. What it does: you upload a short reference video (2–30s) plus a photo of your character, and it generates a new take where your character becomes the lead. How to get a good first result Pick a short clip with one performer, clear movement and a steady camera. Use a clear character photo with a similar pose and framing. Check the credit quote before generating, then review identity, motion, hands and scene consistency. Limits worth knowing: identity, motion, camera and background can drift during generation, and exact face replacement or lip sync isn't guaranteed, so start with one short test. Try it at https://www.castremix.com — feedback welcome in the comments!

articles.title: How I stop an LLM from inventing cloud services
articles.excerpt: Ask a language model for an AWS architecture and you get a confident answer. Sometimes it includes a service that does not exist, a feature that is not real, or a database floating outside any VPC. A…
articles.body: Ask a language model for an AWS architecture and you get a confident answer. Sometimes it includes a service that does not exist, a feature that is not real, or a database floating outside any VPC. A diagram makes this worse, because a clean picture looks more trustworthy than the text it came from. I built CloudArchitect Lite to turn a plain-English description into an AWS diagram. This post is about the three mechanisms that keep the model honest, and what the numbers look like. Version 0.2 is pre-alpha, and I will say where the evidence is thin. You can try a clickable editor in the browser without installing anything: https://aliaksandr-liapin.github.io/cloudarchitect-lite/ . 1. The model can only pick from a catalog The app has a curated catalog of 38 AWS services.

articles.title: Binance Hack DevSecOps Lessons: The Chain Did What It Was Told
articles.excerpt: On October 29, 2026, Binance lost about $6.3 billion. Nobody broke the cryptography, and no consensus bug was involved. The blockchain processed signed transactions exactly as it was designed to. As f…
articles.body: On October 29, 2026, Binance lost about $6.3 billion. Nobody broke the cryptography, and no consensus bug was involved. The blockchain processed signed transactions exactly as it was designed to. As far as the chain could tell, everything was in order. That is the part I keep returning to. The chain did what it was told. Everything that failed happened off-chain: people, laptops, credentials, deploy pipelines, and the policy around signing. Those are platform and DevSecOps problems. Most of us run systems shaped like that, whether or not crypto is involved. This post covers what is publicly known, why a valid signature tells you nothing about intent, and the controls I think platform teams should be building. It ends with a checklist. 1. What happened Here is the public record so far.

articles.title: Whitelabel pages are a bad Jackson inventory
articles.excerpt: Whitelabel pages are a bad Jackson inventory A Spring Boot error page can reveal that an application is running, but it cannot identify the JSON parser version behind that application. This distinctio…
articles.body: Whitelabel pages are a bad Jackson inventory A Spring Boot error page can reveal that an application is running, but it cannot identify the JSON parser version behind that application. This distinction matters after a cluster of jackson-databind vulnerabilities with current fixes for 2.18.9, 2.21.5, 2.22.1, 3.1.5, and 3.2.1, plus later fixes for CVE-2026-68497 in 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2, 3.1.6, and 3.2.2. On November 5, 2026 at 02:50 Beijing time, app="Spring Boot" returned 29,124 matches and http.body="Whitelabel Error Page" returned 2,430,896. Both queries used page 1, page size 1, and sub_type=all . The body expression is roughly two orders of magnitude larger. It can match cached pages, documentation, test fixtures, and services that are not Spring Boot at all.

articles.excerpt: Techniques included laptop infections, compromised internal tooling, and fake job interviews.
articles.body: The hackers who stole billions of dollars in cryptocurrency from the Binance exchange spent months working on the theft and used both social engineering and novel malware in the process, the company said Tuesday. The heist, which both the FBI and the TRM Security firm attributed to North Korean actors, initially targeted $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance wallets. The exchange has since frozen or intercepted $2.85 billion of that sum. Binance said it has set aside funds required to cover the loss and provided this link to a Proof of Reserves page. The $6.34 billion represents the biggest sum ever targeted in a cryptocurrency theft.

articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower peaks tonight — and fireballs could steal the show
articles.excerpt: The Taurid meteor shower could spawn dazzling fireballs in the coming weeks! Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: Heads up stargazers! The Taurid meteor shower is upon us, bringing multiple peaks of activity that could see spectacular shooting stars and fireballs brighten November's sky. Here's where and when to look. What is the Taurid meteor shower(s)? Every autumn, Earth plows through streams of debris left behind by Comet Encke, a 3-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) ice body that orbits the sun once every 3.3 years. These debris streams produce two branches of the Taurid meteor shower : The Southern Taurids, active from Sept. 20 to Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids, active from Oct. 20 to Dec. 10. As Earth plows through the debris streams, tiny particles slam into our atmosphere at 65,000 miles per hour (104,607 kilometers per hour), producing dazzling streaks of light across the night sky.
